title: S2 target grouping-apply settle re-measure on current main
discharges: The follow-up in 2026-08-29-s2-grouping-rebaseline.json to re-measure target/group after #522 and profile the interaction window if the 483.4-vs-401.4 ms gap remained.

scope.note: A pretable-only re-measure of the target-scale `group` settle gap, interleaved with the same target-scale `sort` load-fitness control as the 2026-08-29 milestone.

environment.cleanBuild: Fresh frozen install, dependency rebuild and @pretable/app-bench production build in an isolated worktree; Vite preview on 127.0.0.1:4519 with --strictPort.
environment.method: 7 repeat blocks; each block ran `group` then `sort` by driving apps/bench/tests/bench.spec.ts directly against the external preview server. The traced run was separate and is excluded from n=7.

control.fitnessVerdict: FIT. The 17.1 ms median and 0.9 ms standard deviation match the 2026-08-29 control's 16.8 ms / 0.7 ms within ordinary measurement noise.

interaction.standardDeviation: Sample standard deviation, rounded to 0.1 ms.

comparison.versus2026-08-29: 475.3 ms vs 483.4 ms: -8.1 ms (-1.7%), inside the two runs' observed spread. Current main remains in the re-baselined settle band.
comparison.versus2026-08-10: 475.3 ms vs 401.4 ms: +73.9 ms (+18.4%). The historical target/group settle gap did not close after #522 and the subsequent accessor/identity work.
comparison.verdict: GAP PERSISTS. This is a measured current-main result, not a per-commit attribution.

profile.method: One separate PLAYWRIGHT_PERF_TRACE=1 target/group run, analyzed with scripts/analyze-cdp.mjs and the bench bundle source map. The required interaction view uses --window=interaction; a settle view is included only as diagnostic context.

interactionWindow.finding: The actual top self-time frame is the scroll-reveal layout effect. It is not a height-index replacement frame, and at 11.2% it is not a single-frame explanation for the 73.9 ms cross-date settle delta.

settleWindowContext.note: Reported to show where the full trigger-to-settled interval spends sampled CPU; it does not replace the handoff's required interaction-window attribution.

followUps: Do not attribute the persistent gap to #522 from this aggregate re-measure alone; the current-main band contains all intervening commits.
Any optimization proposal should first isolate the traced settle-window evaluate/GC work or the interaction-window scroll-reveal effect in a dedicated experiment; this milestone proposes no fix.
